cues.en: Instructor: The goal of this video is to define what a data distribution is and show you a bunch of examples of different, well, several examples of different distributions
cues.zh: 這部影片的目標，是定義資料分布，並展示幾種統計中，

cues.en: that are often used in statistics.
cues.zh: 常用的不同分布例子。

cues.en: And I'll end by explaining how distributions are used in statistics and that will set us up for the next series of videos about descriptions of distributions.
cues.zh: 最後解釋統計如何使用分布，為接下來一系列描述分布的影片鋪路。

cues.en: Okay, so we are going to start by thinking about an experiment.
cues.zh: 先想一個實驗。

cues.en: Let's say I do an experiment and what I do is go around and ask a bunch of people, let's say I approach 300 people and I ask them all the same question.
cues.zh: 假設做實驗，四處詢問一群人，例如找300人，問相同問題。

cues.en: How many Slow Loris videos on YouTube, let's say, have you watched?
cues.zh: 你在YouTube看過多少部懶猴影片？

cues.en: Do you know what a Slow Loris is?
cues.zh: 知道懶猴是什麼嗎？

cues.en: If you don't, then I definitely recommend spending a few moments of your time it will greatly enrich your life to watch YouTube videos
cues.zh: 如果不知道，真的建議花一點時間看YouTube上的，

cues.en: of Slow Loris'.
cues.zh: 懶猴影片，會大大豐富你的生活。

cues.en: They're actually primates, so it's an animal.
cues.zh: 它們其實是靈長類動物。

cues.en: A Slow Loris is a primate.
cues.zh: 懶猴是靈長類。

cues.en: So they're actually a little bit related to monkeys and even other greater apes, including humans.
cues.zh: 所以和猴子，甚至包括人類在內的其他大型類人猿，有一點親緣關係。

cues.en: Alright, so we go up to Mr. Orange here and he says he has seen eight Slow Loris videos, which is a pretty respectable number of Slow Loris videos.
cues.zh: 找到橘色先生，他說看過八部懶猴影片，這是很像樣的數量。

cues.en: Then we go up to Mr. Yellow here and Mr. Yellow reports to have seen 14 Slow Loris videos and 298 more.
cues.zh: 再找黃色先生，他說看過十四部，另外還有298人。

cues.en: So we get 300 people in total.
cues.zh: 總共300人。

cues.en: Now, before we even go further, I would like to ask you a question.
cues.zh: 繼續之前，先問一個問題。

cues.en: It's a bit of a pop quiz.
cues.zh: 是個突擊小測驗。

cues.en: What is the data type of this experiment?
cues.zh: 這個實驗的資料類型是什麼？

cues.en: What kind of data are we collecting here?
cues.zh: 蒐集哪種資料？

cues.en: I'm about to reveal my answer, so if you want some more time to think about it or check back in your notes, now is the chance to pause the video.
cues.zh: 馬上揭曉答案。如果想多思考，或翻筆記，現在可以暫停。

cues.en: So I claim that these are ratio data, and I say that these are ratio data for two reasons.
cues.zh: 我認為這是比率資料，有兩個理由。

cues.en: One, these are videos.
cues.zh: 第一，這些是影片。

cues.en: So they're not limited to integer numbers.
cues.zh: 所以不只限於整數。

cues.en: You can stop in the middle of a video and you've watched 0.5 videos.
cues.zh: 可以看到一半停下，就看了0.5部影片。

cues.en: So I think you can stop, you know, I think reporting in integers is done for convenience, but in fact we could really measure this more precisely
cues.zh: 我想，回報整數只是方便，事實上可以更精確測量，

cues.en: and determine that this individual has actually seen 14.7362109 whatever videos about Slow Loris'.
cues.zh: 確認這個人實際看了14.7362109之類的懶猴影片。

cues.en: And furthermore it's ratio and not interval data, because zero is a meaningful number.
cues.zh: 而且是比率，不是區間資料，因為0有意義。

cues.en: You can actually have watched zero videos about Slow Loris', and that really means the absence of having experienced the joy of Slow Loris YouTube videos.
cues.zh: 確實可能看過0部懶猴影片，那真的代表完全沒有體驗YouTube懶猴影片的樂趣。

cues.en: Okay, anyway, so what would we do?
cues.zh: 總之，接著怎麼做？

cues.en: What would you do to have a look at these data?
cues.zh: 你會怎麼觀察資料？

cues.en: If I said, you know, now I give you this data set, 300 points and now I told you to visualize these data, what would you pick?
cues.zh: 如果現在把300個資料點給你，要你視覺化，會選什麼？

cues.en: What kind of visualization would you go with?
cues.zh: 會用哪種視覺化？

cues.en: Well, I guess you would probably go with a histogram and it might look something like this.
cues.zh: 我猜你大概選直方圖，可能長這樣。

cues.en: We have the number of videos watched on the X-axis discretized at some, you know, reasonable level of disco discretization.
cues.zh: x軸是看過的影片數，採用某種合理程度的離散化。

cues.en: And then on the Y-axis we have the count, the number of people who have seen that many videos.
cues.zh: y軸是次數，也就是看過那麼多影片的人數。

cues.en: Maybe you could convert this into proportion, but that doesn't actually change the shape.
cues.zh: 也許能轉成比例，但不改變形狀。

cues.en: So we might get a distribution that looks something like this.
cues.zh: 分布可能像這樣。

cues.en: Maybe there's an outlier up here, some specific individual won't be named, happens to watch a lot of Slow Loris videos and seems to have seen more than most other people.
cues.zh: 這裡也許有離群值，某位不透露姓名的人，剛好看很多懶猴影片，比大多數人看得多。

cues.en: Now this is a histogram and this describes a data distribution.
cues.zh: 這是直方圖，描述資料分布。

cues.en: So a data distribution is basically just a histogram, except what we are interested in is not the histogram per se, but some features of the shape of the histogram.
cues.zh: 資料分布基本上就是直方圖，但我們關心的，不是直方圖本身，而是形狀的某些特徵。

cues.en: So in fact, we could draw a line that would go through this histogram like this.
cues.zh: 其實可以像這樣，畫一條穿過直方圖的線。

cues.en: Maybe we have to account for this outlier here.
cues.zh: 也許要把這個離群值納入考量。

cues.en: And this line here describes a distribution.
cues.zh: 這條線描述一個分布。

cues.en: And then what we want to do with data distributions is come up with some simple mathematical formulas that allow us to characterize the ideal distribution
cues.zh: 接著希望用簡單數學公式，刻畫某種理想分布，

cues.en: that this histogram might be an approximation, an empirical approximation of.
cues.zh: 這張直方圖，可能是它的經驗近似。

cues.en: In this specific case, this looks to me like what's called a power-law distribution, not this outlier notwithstanding.
cues.zh: 這個例子，看起來像冪律分布，先不管這個離群值。

cues.en: So a power-law distribution refers to a characteristic of a data set where the number of occurrences is inversely proportional
cues.zh: 冪律分布，指資料集的一種特徵：出現次數，

cues.en: or inversely related to the magnitude of, or the count of those occurrences.
cues.zh: 與這些事件的大小或數量，成反比，或呈反向關係。

cues.en: This is also something you see, for example, with earthquakes.
cues.zh: 例如地震也會看到。

cues.en: If you measure earthquake magnitudes by earthquake frequency, you would find that there's a really large number of very weak earthquakes,
cues.zh: 觀察地震規模與發生頻率，會發現很微弱的地震非常多，

cues.en: and as the earthquakes get stronger and stronger in magnitude, there's fewer and fewer of them.
cues.zh: 規模越強，數量越少。

cues.en: So that's called a power law distribution.
cues.zh: 這叫冪律分布。

cues.en: And this is just an example.
cues.zh: 這只是例子。

cues.en: Obviously I'm making up all these data, although I do recommend watching some Slow Loris videos.
cues.zh: 顯然，資料都是編造的，不過確實建議看些懶猴影片。

cues.en: Okay, so that's a power law distribution.
cues.zh: 以上是冪律分布。

cues.en: Here's some examples of a few other distributions.
cues.zh: 再看其他幾種分布。

cues.en: This one is called a Gaussian distribution.
cues.zh: 這叫高斯分布。

cues.en: It's also called the bell curve.
cues.zh: 也叫鐘形曲線。

cues.en: It is possibly the most famous, most important, most influential and most widely used distribution in certainly all of statistics,
cues.zh: 它可能是整個統計領域，最知名、最重要、最有影響力、最廣泛使用的分布，

cues.en: probably all of applied mathematics.
cues.zh: 甚至整個應用數學也如此。

cues.en: And I will talk much, much more about Gaussian distributions and how they're used throughout the course.
cues.zh: 整門課會更深入談高斯分布及其用途。

cues.en: Then we also have something called a T distribution.
cues.zh: 接著是t分布。

cues.en: This is for evaluating the statistical significance of T values.
cues.zh: 用來評估t值的統計顯著性。

cues.en: So I'll talk more about this in a section on T statistics and T test.
cues.zh: t統計量與t檢定那一節，會再談。

cues.en: Here's what's called an F distribution.
cues.zh: 這叫F分布。

cues.en: This is important for general linear models like ANOVA's and regressions, and this is something called a chi-square distribution.
cues.zh: 對ANOVA與迴歸等一般線性模型很重要。這個則是卡方分布。

cues.en: This looks like an X, but it's actually the Greek letter Chi, so it's a chi-square distribution.
cues.zh: 看起來像X，但其實是希臘字母χ，所以是χ平方分布。

cues.en: You can see that a lot of these distributions look kind of similar in some sense.
cues.zh: 可以看到，這些分布某種程度看起來很像。

cues.en: They're smooth, that's one characteristic of these kinds of data distributions that are used in inferential statistics.
cues.zh: 都平滑，這是推論統計使用的這些資料分布的一個特徵。

cues.en: There are other distributions that are not smooth, that have sharp edges like a uniform distribution for example, and they often taper down
cues.zh: 也有不平滑、有尖銳邊緣的分布，例如均勻分布。而且它們經常會逐漸下降，

cues.en: as X goes to minus infinity or plus infinity.
cues.zh: 當x趨近負無限大或正無限大。

cues.en: Some of these distributions are defined for negative values and for positive values like the Gaussian and the T.
cues.zh: 有些分布對負值、正值都有定義，例如高斯與t分布。

cues.en: And F and chi-square are two examples of distributions that are only defined for positive values.
cues.zh: F與卡方則是只對正值定義的兩個例子。

cues.en: So zero would be here.
cues.zh: 所以0在這裡。

cues.en: There's no negative F values and there's no negative chi-square values that should already be obvious from the fact that it's squared here.
cues.zh: 沒有負的F值，也沒有負的卡方值。這裡有平方，應該已經很明顯。

cues.en: Now there's many, many, many distributions that are used in statistics.
cues.zh: 統計中有非常非常多分布。

cues.en: I'm just showing you these four as an example of the more common ones.
cues.zh: 只展示四個較常見的例子。

cues.en: So you can see just a little bit what they look like, what these distributions look like.
cues.zh: 讓你稍微看看這些分布的樣子。

cues.en: So why do we care about distributions?
cues.zh: 為什麼關心分布？

cues.en: Well, most statistical procedures in particular, inferential statistical techniques are based on assumptions about distributions.
cues.zh: 大多數統計程序，尤其推論統計技術，都基於分布假設。

cues.en: So when you are evaluating the statistical significance of some test, what you're actually doing is making assumptions that the parameters
cues.zh: 評估某個檢定的統計顯著性時，其實是在假設參數，

cues.en: look something like this or something like this, depending of course on which specific statistic you are looking at.
cues.zh: 大致像這個或這個，當然取決於具體看哪個統計量。

cues.en: So understanding these distributions is necessary for appropriately applying different inferential statistical procedures.
cues.zh: 所以理解分布，是適當應用不同推論統計程序的必要條件。

cues.en: So these two points are really just about the practicalities of doing inferential statistics, but data distributions and theoretical distributions are important
cues.zh: 這兩點只是做推論統計的實務面，但資料分布與理論分布，

cues.en: also for theoretical science as well.
cues.zh: 對理論科學也很重要。

cues.en: Data distributions are used to provide insights into the fundamental nature of nature itself into biology and physics and chemistry.
cues.zh: 資料分布能幫助理解大自然本質，包括生物、物理與化學。

cues.en: Scientists use distributions to try and understand nature, and I already gave you one example a few slides ago with the power law distribution and using power law distributions
cues.zh: 科學家用分布理解自然。前幾張已經舉過冪律分布例子，用它，

cues.en: to try and understand something fundamental about the nature of earthquakes.
cues.zh: 嘗試理解地震本質的一些根本特性。

cues.en: And people who do modeling of biological systems and physical systems are often using distributions to simulate various kinds of dynamics in physical
cues.zh: 為生物與物理系統建模的人，也經常用分布，模擬物理，

cues.en: and biological systems.
cues.zh: 與生物系統的各種動態。

cues.en: Okay, so now I want to say a few more things about the qualities or characteristics of distributions, and this is gonna set us up for the next half dozen
cues.zh: 現在再談幾個分布的性質、特徵，為接下來大約六部，

cues.en: or 10 videos or so.
cues.zh: 或十部影片鋪路。

cues.en: Okay, so what I have plotted here is three different Gaussian distributions and you can see that they all have kind of the same shape roughly.
cues.zh: 這裡畫三個不同高斯分布，形狀大致相同。

cues.en: You know, they all start at zero or close to zero.
cues.zh: 從0，或接近0開始。

cues.en: They go up, they peak, and then they go back down.
cues.zh: 上升、到頂峰，再下降。

cues.en: But they also differ in important characteristics.
cues.zh: 但重要特徵也有差異。

cues.en: For example, where the peak is, you can see the peak is to the left for this orange distribution.
cues.zh: 例如峰的位置，橘色分布的峰偏左。

cues.en: And the peak is exactly the same for these two, the green and the blue distributions.
cues.zh: 綠色與藍色這兩個，峰的位置完全相同。

cues.en: So there's something about the peaks of distributions that we are going to want to quantify.
cues.zh: 所以我們想量化分布峰的某些特性。

cues.en: We're gonna wanna come up with a single number that characterizes this peak.
cues.zh: 想找一個數，刻畫這個峰。

cues.en: Obviously it's gonna be the location on the X-axis where that peak occurs.
cues.zh: 顯然，就是峰出現的x軸位置。

cues.en: Talk more about that later.
cues.zh: 之後會詳談。

cues.en: And then there's also measures of the width of this distribution.
cues.zh: 也有衡量分布寬度的量。

cues.en: So you can see the orange and the blue distribution are equally wide.
cues.zh: 橘色與藍色分布一樣寬。

cues.en: You can imagine drawing a line through like for example, halfway from the base to the peak.
cues.zh: 可以想像，例如在底部到頂峰一半高度，畫一條線。

cues.en: And you know, you might call that full width at half maximum, but the terminology doesn't matter for now.
cues.zh: 可以叫半高全寬，但目前術語不重要。

cues.en: The point is that there's something about the width of these distributions that tells us about the distributions and tells us about the data that are underlying these distributions.
cues.zh: 重點是，分布寬度會告訴我們分布本身，以及底層資料的某些資訊。

cues.en: So these are measures of dispersion and I'm also going to talk more about these in a few videos from now.
cues.zh: 這些是離散程度的量，再過幾部影片也會談。

cues.en: Okay, and then just a little bit of terminology.
cues.zh: 再介紹一點術語。

cues.en: If you have a distribution that looks like this, so it has one peak, then you call that a unimodal distribution.
cues.zh: 如果分布像這樣，只有一個峰，叫單峰分布。

cues.en: These are called the modes of the distribution.
cues.zh: 這些叫分布的峰，也就是mode。

cues.en: And a distribution that looks like this will be called bimodal.
cues.zh: 這種樣子的分布，叫雙峰分布。

cues.en: More generally, you can call these multimodal distribution.
cues.zh: 更一般地，叫多峰分布。

cues.en: So if there's more than one mode, if there's more than one peak, then you can call that a multimodal distribution.
cues.zh: 如果超過一個mode、超過一個峰，就能叫多峰分布。

cues.en: So bimodal would be this case.
cues.zh: 雙峰是這個例子。

cues.en: You could also have a trimodal distribution and so on.
cues.zh: 也能有三峰分布，依此類推。

cues.en: So in this video I explained what a data distribution is.
cues.zh: 這部影片解釋資料分布是什麼。

cues.en: It's essentially the shape of a histogram when you sample the histogram finely enough.
cues.zh: 基本上，是以足夠精細區間取樣後，直方圖的形狀。

cues.en: I showed you some examples of different distributions that are commonly used in statistics, and I talked a little bit about why these data distributions are important
cues.zh: 展示統計常用的不同分布例子，也稍微談為什麼資料分布，

cues.en: in statistics and in science more generally.
cues.zh: 對統計與更一般的科學重要。

cues.en: And I gave you some visual intuition into some of the quantitative measures of distributions that we are going to start extracting over the next several videos.
cues.zh: 並給你一些視覺直覺，了解接下來幾部影片，要開始擷取的分布定量指標。
